messages.text: there is no yt video from gekko buddy

Right — the KBuddy's too new for reviews; GekkoScience only put it back on sale last week. The K. is the one with footage out there, and the KBuddy is the same build philosophy, US-made.

$500, 15–18 TH/s, ships December 1. Want me to pull its exact wall watts so we can price it at your 12 cents?

to check how noisy it is
as the b30 is noisy as hell or magic miner
Read the gekkoscience kbuddy 15 th s page

No published dB numbers on any of them, so I won't invent one. But watts tell you most of it: the KBuddy runs 15 TH at 200 W stock, fully enclosed steel case with speed-controlled fans — that's the quietest of the three by a distance. The 40T at 650 W is a real fan unit, and the B30 at 30 TH was re-cooled to be quieter but still isn't living-room quiet.

Where would it sit?
yeah living room

Then the KBuddy is your machine. In a living room the B30 and the 40T will annoy you within a week; 200 W of enclosed, speed-controlled fans you can sit next to.

At your 12 cents: about $17 a month at 15 TH stock, $26 at 18 TH max. $500, ships December 1, 2026. It ships from the US, so 21% import VAT lands on delivery.

Want it carted?
how much watt at 18th

300 W at 18 TH/s — that's the max clock. Stock is 15 TH at 200 W, and with tuning the listing says you can get down to 13 J/TH.

At 300 W and 12 cents that's about $26 a month. Fans will be louder at max than at stock, so in a living room most people sit at 15 TH.

Shall I cart one?
what i need to tune

Nothing you build — it's in the web interface. High, Medium and Low presets out of the box, plus sliders for hashrate, efficiency and heat if you want to go past the presets. Onboard telemetry handles the voltage itself. There's even a remote for the power mode.

So: plug in, open it in a browser, pick Low or Medium for the living room.
does it come directly with harlo that i can preset to turn of at night in eco mode automatic

No — Harlo OS is the Harlo units' software. The K. runs GekkoScience's own Linux controller with its own web interface.

The presets are there, but the listing doesn't claim a built-in time scheduler, so I won't promise one. What people actually do for night eco is a smart plug or a timer on the socket, or just leave it at Low 24/7 — at 200 W that's $17 a month at your rate, cheap enough to not bother switching.

Want me to get JD to confirm whether there's a schedule function in the UI?
yes i need confirm becouse on day i can run full and at night eco mode but of course dont wanna do this manually
Handed to the team · Cannot confirm from the listing whether the KBuddy controller supports time-base

JD has it — the exact question: does the KBuddy UI let you schedule full by day and eco at night automatically. He'll confirm here, or by email to (email hidden) if you step away.

Fallback if the answer is no: a €15 smart plug with a timer does day/night switching, though it cuts power rather than dropping modes.
is there any other miner i can run at day max 900 watt but at night max 300 watt

Nothing we sell spans that in one box. The Magic Miner 40T is the widest range: 30 TH at 450 W, 40 at 650, 50 at 850 — so it hits your 900 ceiling but its floor is 450 W, not 300.

The combination that actually fits: KBuddy at 200 W running 24/7 in the living room, and a 40T in a garage or utility room for the solar hours. At 850 W it's not a living-room machine.

Do you have somewhere else it could sit?
so magic miner cant be run lower then 450 watt

450 W is the lowest published preset, yes. Whether the firmware lets you tune below it isn't something I'll guess at.

JD's already on your KBuddy question, so I'll put this in the same thread: can the 40T be clocked under 450 W, and does either unit schedule modes by time.

For now the honest picture: 40T floor 450 W, KBuddy floor 200 W. Only the KBuddy goes where you want at night.
i realy like the magic miner, but i need to know how many watt at lowest i can run with how much th
Read the magic miner 40t page

Lowest documented mode is Eco: 30 TH/s at 450 W, ~50 dB. That's the floor the manufacturer publishes — nothing below it, and JD will say whether the firmware goes lower.

Two things from the live listing worth knowing: Turbo 50 TH at 850 W is an overclock and voids the warranty, and 50 dB in Eco is audible in a living room.

Eco at your 12 cents is about $39 a month. $799, ships November 21, 2026.
any other options
Read the bsb b30 page
Read the hammer miner thor p2 page

Quietest first, from the live listings:

Thor P2 — 10 TH at 166 W, ~40 dB, $369. The living-room-friendly one. Ships October 3, 2026.

KBuddy — 15 TH at 200 W, enclosed steel case, $500. Ships December 1, 2026.

Harlo B30 — 30 TH at 360–450 W, ~50 dB, $899.

For your day/night split, two P2s on separate plugs gives you 332 W full and 166 W at night, both silent-ish. Which direction appeals?
b30 is too loud

Agreed — 50 dB is fridge-level and it never stops. Same figure as the 40T in Eco, which is why neither belongs next to a sofa.

So it's the KBuddy or the Thor P2. For your case I'd take the KBuddy: 15 TH at 200 W is 50% more hashrate than the P2 for $131 more, fully enclosed steel, and it has the Low/Medium/High modes you want for day and night. $500, ships December 1, 2026.

Cart it?
what is with the bad news about bs 4 company

What I can state: BitFortun is off sale across the board since September 20 while they fix firmware that reported a higher hashrate than the unit actually delivered. The B.1 and BS-2 listings were corrected down to true numbers on the 25th. That's the same correction that likely explains your 22 vs 18 on the BS-4.

And a correction from me: the BS-4 drop is mid-October, no exact day confirmed. I shouldn't have said the 4th.

Anything beyond that about the company I don't know and won't guess.
so the commpany is not trustful?

I wouldn't put it that way. They shipped firmware that overstated hashrate, and then they pulled every product off sale and corrected the numbers down rather than keep selling. That second part is the part I'd weigh.

What it does mean: their dates and specs have moved, so I'd not plan around a BS-4 you can't buy.

The K. is a US-built unit, specs published, $500, ships December 1. That's the one I'd put in your living room.
what modes does bs 4 runs
Read the bitfortun bs 4 page

The live listing publishes no mode table — just one rated point: 18 TH/s, ~300 W, ~50 dB, water cooled, 4x BM1373, $599.99.

And that answers your earlier question: the record now reads 18 TH/s, not 22. That's the correction landing, same as BS-1 and BS-2. JD will still confirm it in writing to your email.

Note the 50 dB too — same as the B30 you just ruled out. For a living room that's the KBuddy, not this.
why its so load its watercooled

Water cooling moves the heat, it doesn't remove it. The loop carries 300 W out to a radiator, and that radiator still needs fans blowing through it — the listing shows dual fan headers — plus a pump humming the whole time.

So you trade a loud little fan on a heatsink for a quieter-but-constant fan plus pump. Usually about a wash, which is what their 50 dB reflects.

The K. gets quiet by using less power: 200 W, not 300.
so kbuddy is 200 watt 15 th right

Correct. Stock setting is 15 TH/s at 200 W, max clock 18 TH/s at 300 W, and the listing says tuning can get it to 13 J/TH.

One honest gap: GekkoScience publishes no dB figure for it. "Quiet integrated fans with speed control" is their claim, and 200 W in a sealed steel case is a good sign, but I can't give you a number like I can for the others.

$500, ships December 1, 2026. Want it carted?

Handed to the team · Two KBuddy specs not on the listing are the shopper's deciding factors: measured

Both are now with JD as one question: the measured dB at 15 TH and at 18 TH, and whether the UI schedules modes by time. He's on right now, so stay in the chat if you can — otherwise it goes to (email hidden)

Nothing's lost by waiting either: it ships December 1 regardless, and it isn't a drop that sells out in minutes.
how important is to have the miner directly lan coneccted

Not critical. Pool mining sends tiny packets every few seconds, so bandwidth is irrelevant — what matters is the connection not dropping.

Ethernet is simply more reliable: no re-auth, no congestion at 2.4 GHz, so fewer stale shares. Wi-Fi costs you maybe a fraction of a percent if the signal is decent.

The K. does both, including 5 GHz, which most of these units don't. In a living room with good signal, Wi-Fi is fine.
i want lottery mining
Ran the power-cost calculator · 12¢/kWh

Then hashrate is your ticket count — odds scale straight off TH/s, nothing else.

Which puts your two wants in tension: the KBuddy's 15–18 TH is the quiet choice, the 40T's 40 TH is more than double the tickets for $799 but 50 dB at best.

Solo also means long dry spells with zero payouts, which is the point — you own the machine and the draw repeats every ten minutes for years.

Is the living room fixed, or is there a hallway or cupboard it could live in?
is internet for lottery very iportant

More than for pool mining, but still not demanding. Two things matter.

Uptime: if the connection drops, the miner has no work and you're buying zero tickets for that period.

Latency: when someone else finds a block, you want the new template fast. Hashing a few seconds on the old one is wasted. Milliseconds-level stuff, any normal home line handles it.

Bandwidth is trivial. A stable Wi-Fi signal is enough; ethernet just removes the drop risk.

Ja, einer: die KBOX von GekkoScience, $800. Gleicher Hersteller, gleiches geschlossenes Stahlgehäuse, aber mit drei festen Stufen — Low 10 TH, Medium 16 TH, High 22 TH bei 330 W. Das ist genau Ihr Tag/Nacht-Wechsel in einem Gerät.

Der NerdOctaxe (12 TH, ~200 W, $359.99) ist für EU-Adressen gerade nicht bestellbar, nur UK-Stecker.
